data.title: Basis steady, weather favors planting progress
data.description:
Basis bids for hard red winter wheat were unchanged in the southern US Plains on Friday, spot checks showed, and cash markets were quiet as wheat futures dropped and farmers focused on planting the 2027 winter wheat crop, merchandisers said.

  • Warm and dry weather this week has helped accelerate seeding following heavy rains at the start of the month. "Guys are running hard, putting wheat in the ground," one Oklahoma merchandiser said.

  • High temperatures neared 90 degrees Fahrenheit (32 degrees Celsius) on Friday as far north as South Dakota.

  • "Warmth is ideal for the germination and establishment of recently planted winter grains, especially in areas noting recent improvements in topsoil moisture," the US Department of Agriculture said in a daily weather note.

  • K.C. December hard red winter wheat (KWZ26) futures settled down 17 cents on Friday, or 2.3%, at $7.19-1/4 per bushel after hitting $7.09, the contract's lowest since mid-July.

  • Wheat fell in sympathy with corn and soybean futures after the USDA hiked its 2026 US harvest outlook.

  • The USDA also raised its forecast of US 2026/27 wheat ending stocks to 740 million bushels, up from 717 million last month and above the average analyst estimate of 721 million.

  • Protein premiums were mixed. Premiums for railcar wheat to and through Kansas City fell by 7 cents a bushel for wheat with 12.0% and 12.2% protein, but premiums rose by 2 to 4 cents a bushel for wheat with 12.6% through 13.0% protein content.

data.title: Brazil's CSN signs term sheet to sell German unit to Spain's Megasa for $616 million
data.description:
Brazilian steelmaker CSN said on Friday it had signed a binding term sheet to sell Germany-based unit Stahlwerk Thüringen GmbH to the controlling shareholder of Spanish industrial group Megasa for an enterprise value of €550 million ($616 million).

CSN said in a securities filing that the term sheet sets the key terms and conditions for a deal and provides for an exclusivity period of up to 10 weeks to negotiate the definitive terms.

  • The German unit, known as SWT, is a long steel producer with an installed production capacity of 1.1 million metric tons of steel per year

  • CSN said the potential sale represents "another important step" in its divestment program aimed at reducing its current debt leverage

  • CSN acquired the German unit in 2012 in a €482.5 million deal

($1 = 0.8928 euros)

data.title: Verizon, AT&T And T-Mobile Shares Tumble As SpaceX Strikes C
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Shares of major US telecommunications companies fell sharply on Friday after Elon Musk's SpaceX agreed to acquire a nationwide wireless spectrum portfolio from private-equity firm Grain Management, strengthening its plans to expand Starlink into mobile services.

Verizon shares dropped around 10 percent, putting them on track for their steepest single-day decline since 2002. T-Mobile fell 13 percent, its worst potential daily performance since 2013, while AT&T lost approximately 10 percent, marking its biggest decline since 2000. SpaceX shares rose around 1 percent.

The deal covers Grain Management's nationwide portfolio of 800 MHz spectrum licences, comprising up to 14 megahertz of paired spectrum. The Wall Street Journal reported that SpaceX would pay approximately $8 billion in cash, although the companies did not disclose the financial terms.

The acquisition could help Starlink Mobile improve connectivity inside buildings and in areas where conventional mobile networks struggle.

Low-band spectrum travels longer distances and penetrates obstacles more effectively than higher-frequency signals, potentially strengthening SpaceX's ability to deliver satellite connectivity directly to standard mobile phones.

The transaction remains subject to approval by the Federal Communications Commission (FCC). FCC Chair Brendan Carr described increased competition in the spectrum market as positive for American consumers, adding that the market would determine which providers succeed.

Analysts at Evercore ISI said the acquisition gives SpaceX the foundations of a more developed network, while JPMorgan said it makes Starlink Mobile's long-term opportunity more credible.

However, analysts cautioned that established wireless carriers face limited near-term risk because building a competitive network requires considerable time, infrastructure and capital.

data.title: As Yields Surged, Small-Cap Stocks Were Hit Hard — WSJ
data.description:
By Vicky Ge Huang

As bond yields march higher, small companies are taking the brunt of the damage.

The Russell 2000 index, which tracks shares of smaller companies, fell for a fifth-straight week, its longest weekly losing streak since May 2022. The index was lower by 0.9% this week and down 5.7% over the five-week span. The decline is a stark departure from the first half of this year, when small caps had their biggest run in decades.

Investors are worried that surging Treasury yields will hit small companies where it hurts most: their borrowing costs. Unlike large multinationals, smaller companies typically have limited access to capital markets and rely on short-term or floating-rate loans that track rates set by the Federal Reserve. At the same time, the profits of many of these businesses are already under pressure thanks to the rising cost of fuel and other goods.

"You are kind of getting that dual squeeze," said David Miller, chief investment officer and senior portfolio manager at Catalyst Funds. "As your borrowing costs go up, your margins go down."

The yield on the 10-year Treasury note, which influences interest rates across the economy, settled at 5.243% Friday after touching a fresh 24-year high earlier this week.

What's worse, a rising proportion of small companies' long-term debt comes due over the next five years, which means they would need to be refinanced at higher rates, according to a recent research note from Bank of America. Last month, the central bank raised interest rates for the first time in three years, and investors expect further hikes to rein in inflation.

Since the Russell 2000's weekly losing streak began, healthcare and consumer discretionary stocks have been among the hardest hit. Early-stage biotech companies borrow heavily to fund clinical trials long before making a profit. Meanwhile, consumer-facing companies have been squeezed as higher borrowing costs and sticky inflation erode household purchasing power.

Shares of biopharmaceutical company Caribou Biosciences fell 62% this week after announcing it is exploring strategic alternatives and cutting jobs. Neighborhood Intelligence, the company previously known as Bed, Bath and Beyond, dropped 39%.

Gains by many of the benchmark indexes have been heavily concentrated in a relatively small number of stocks, with many others flat or falling.

"More than half of the small-cap index is below its 52-week high by more than 20%, so a lot of these stocks are in corrections or mini-bear markets of their own," said Jeff Blazek, co-chief investment officer of multiasset strategies at Neuberger, which recently downgraded small-cap stocks to "target weight" after about three years of being "overweight" on smaller stocks.

Blazek added that many of last year's outperforming small-cap AI stocks have since graduated to midcap and large-cap indexes, removing key growth drivers and further weighing on the Russell 2000s recent performance.

On Friday, the S&P 500 rose 0.6%, and the Nasdaq gained 0.6%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 423 points, or 0.8%. All three indexes closed in the green for the week.

Small-caps' recent stretch of underperformance might be good news for bargain hunters. The valuations of small-cap stocks have dropped significantly, and are now below their historical averages during times when interest rates were 5% to 7%, according to analysts at Bank of America. The bank expects 10-year yield to settle at around 5% by the end of the year, adding that small-cap stocks could rebound if rates peak soon.

"Because rates are trading so much in sympathy with oil, and oil is trading so much related to Iran," said Blazek, "a favorable yield environment or a resolution to the Iran war, those would probably encourage at least short-term outperformance of small-caps."

Write to Vicky Ge Huang at vicky.huang@wsj.com

data.title: Former OpenAI Researchers Claim They Were Fired After Raising AI Safety Concerns
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Three former OpenAI researchers have disputed the company's explanation for their dismissals, alleging they were fired after raising concerns about artificial intelligence safety rather than for mishandling sensitive information.

Mikita Balesni, Tomek Korbak and Jasmine Wang, who previously worked in safety and alignment roles, said in an open letter that their departures could discourage employees from speaking up about risks associated with advanced AI systems. Balesni said he believed they were dismissed for prioritising safety over the company's short-term corporate interests.

Korbak claimed he had repeatedly raised concerns about losing the ability to monitor the internal reasoning of AI agents, which he described as an important tool for detecting misbehaviour.

OpenAI rejected the allegations, saying an internal investigation found that the researchers had mishandled sensitive information outside established procedures. The company maintained that their dismissals were unrelated to raising safety concerns and said it stood by its decision.

The dispute comes amid growing debate over AI safety and the ability of technology companies to monitor increasingly capable systems. OpenAI said it was finalising agreements with independent safety assessors and planned to announce further details in the coming weeks.

data.title: CME feeder cattle hit 3-month peak after corn price plunge
data.description:
By Karl Plume

Chicago Mercantile Exchange feeder cattle futures rallied to a three-month high on Friday after the US Department of Agriculture unexpectedly raised its 2026 US corn harvest outlook, sending prices for the feed grain down sharply.

Live cattle futures followed feeders higher and hit a two-month peak, with technical buying giving the market an additional lift.

The USDA said in a monthly crop report on Friday it expects US farmers to harvest their second-largest crop on record despite adverse summer weather that had most traders anticipating a cut to its production estimate.

Corn futures tumbled by as much as their daily 30-cent-per-bushel trading limit following the report, sending feeder cattle higher on the prospect of lower costs for their biggest input.

"The feeder cattle market is loving this," said Ross Baldwin, broker and market analyst at John Stewart and Associates. "You get out to the deferred months, and it's as bullish as you can imagine."

CME November feeder cattle finished the day up 7.075 cents, or 2.1%, at 341.950 cents per pound. The benchmark contract held underlying technical chart support at its 100-day moving average but hit overhead resistance at its 200-day average.

December live cattle settled up 3.500 cents, or 1.6%, at 227.050 cents per pound after breaking through overhead technical resistance at its 100-day moving average.

Cattle futures had come under pressure this week from sluggish cash market trading and a downturn in wholesale beef prices.

The USDA on Friday quoted the choice boxed beef cutout at $373.35 per hundredweight, down $1.50 from a day earlier.

Meanwhile, CME lean hog futures ended lower on Friday for the fourth straight session, anchored by weak cash hog and pork prices.

Most-active December hogs (LHZ26) fell to a contract low of 67.325 cents per pound and settled 0.775 cent lower at 67.825 cents per pound.

data.title: Biopharmaceutical Company Bambusa Therapeutics Files for IPO
data.description:
By Stephen Nakrosis

Biopharmaceutical company Bambusa Therapeutics filed for an initial public offering, and said it applied to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol BBTX.

The company said it is working to develop bispecific antibodies designed to redefine standards of care in immunology and inflammation.

Bambusa said it is currently evaluating its lead product candidate, BBT001 for the treatment of moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis, in the U.S., Australia, Europe, and New Zealand. The company also said it initiated a Phase 2a clinical trial of BBT001 to treat chronic spontaneous urticaria in China.

Salvia Investment and entities affiliated with RA Capital and with Biotechnology Value Fund are listed among the company's principal stockholders.

The company also said to date it has generated no revenue, and had an accumulated deficit of $77.2 million as of June 30.

The company didn't provide an expected size for its IPO, nor did it offer an expected price range for shares.

Write to Stephen Nakrosis at stephen.nakrosis@wsj.com

data.title: Retension Pharmaceuticals, Clinical-Stage Developer of Hypertension Therapies, Files for Nasdaq Capital Market IPO
data.description:
Retension Pharmaceuticals, a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on hypertension, filed a final prospectus for its initial public offering. The company’s common stock will trade on the Nasdaq Capital Market under the ticker RTSN at $12.00 per share. The IPO comprises 3,750,000 shares, raising gross proceeds of $45 million.

Business Description

Retension Pharmaceuticals is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing RTN-001, a next‑generation, once‑daily, oral PDE‑5 inhibitor designed to enhance nitric oxide–cGMP signaling to lower blood pressure. Unlike first‑generation PDE‑5 inhibitors, RTN‑001 was engineered for improved bioavailability and distribution to cardiovascular smooth muscle, aiming to deliver sustained reductions in both peripheral and central blood pressure with a modified‑release formulation.

The company is advancing RTN‑001 for patients with uncontrolled and resistant hypertension, populations that remain inadequately served despite widespread availability of existing antihypertensives. RTN‑001 has been evaluated across nine completed clinical studies (including two Phase 2 pilot trials) with 243 participants, demonstrating clinically meaningful placebo‑adjusted blood pressure reductions and a tolerability profile consistent with the PDE‑5 class. A randomized, double‑blind, placebo‑controlled Phase 2b dose‑ranging trial in uncontrolled hypertension is ongoing, with initial data expected in the first half of 2027.

Market Overview

  • Total addressable market: An estimated 1.4 billion adults with hypertension globally and ~120 million U.S. adults
  • Market growth: Lower treatment targets and unmet control rates expand candidate pools for new therapies
  • Market position: Focus on nitric oxide–cGMP pathway with a next-generation PDE-5 inhibitor targeting uncontrolled and resistant hypertension
  • Key competitors: Multiple generic antihypertensives; indirect competition from classes such as ACE inhibitors, ARBs, calcium channel blockers, diuretics, beta blockers, MRAs
  • Industry trends: FDA guidance recognizes blood pressure reduction as an approvable surrogate endpoint, often reducing need for pre‑approval outcomes trials

Operational Metrics

  • Customers: Pre-commercial; no product revenue to date
  • Locations: Approximately 31 U.S. clinical sites in the ongoing Phase 2b trial
  • Geographic presence: United States clinical operations; prior trials conducted in the UK and Germany
  • Partnerships: Exclusive sublicense for RTN‑001 via Redux/Kadmon; third‑party CMOs and CROs for manufacturing and trials
  • Orders/GMV: Not applicable (biopharma R&D stage)
  • Other key metrics: 9 completed clinical trials; 243 participants dosed historically; ~40% Phase 2b enrollment as of September 11, 2026; initial Phase 2b data expected H1 2027; crystalline polymorph patent protection expected through at least 2044

Financials Highlights

  • Revenue (current): No revenue (pre-commercial)
  • Operating income: -$7.8 million (loss from operations, six months ended June 30, 2026)
  • Net income: -$7.5 million (six months ended June 30, 2026); -$6.3 million (FY 2025)

Management

  • Eric Keller, Chief Executive Officer - Biopharma executive and dealmaker; previously led asset licensing and development initiatives at Nano Terra and affiliates.
  • Alex Schwartz, Chief Financial Officer - Biopharma finance and IR leader with roles at Ventyx, Allakos, NGM Biopharmaceuticals, and Esperion; former biotech equity research analyst.
  • Paul Sweetnam, Ph.D., Chief Scientific Officer - Drug discovery leader; previously CSO at Surface Logix where RTN‑001 originated; senior R&D roles at Bayer and Pfizer.
  • Alison D. Schecter, M.D., Chief Medical Officer - Clinical development executive with hypertension and cardiovascular experience at Mineralys, Sanofi‑Genzyme, Baxalta/Shire, and others.
  • Sabine Bisson, Ph.D., Chief Operating Officer - Development operations and portfolio leader with experience at Regeneron, Cellectis, and Volastra across oncology and cardiometabolic programs.
  • Michael J. Berendt, Ph.D., Chairman of the Board - Former pharma R&D head (Bayer, Pfizer) and biotech CEO; extensive governance and transaction experience.
  • Franklin M. Berger, Director - Veteran biotech investor and former Wall Street analyst; multiple public company directorships.
  • Donald Olds, M.B.A., Director - Life sciences executive and director; former CEO of NEOMED Institute; extensive board experience.

IPO Structure

  • Issuer: Retension Pharmaceuticals, Inc.
  • Filing date: October 09, 2026
  • Proposed ticker: RTSN
  • Exchange: Nasdaq Capital Market
  • Price range: $12.00 per share
  • Offering size: $45,000,000
  • Shares offered: 3,750,000 shares
  • Lead underwriters: Leerink Partners, Guggenheim Securities, Oppenheimer & Co., Titan Partners
  • Use of proceeds: Complete the Phase 2b trial of RTN-001 in uncontrolled hypertension, prepare/support and advance a planned Phase 3, and for general corporate purposes.

data.title: Gran Tierra Energy expects $315M cash from $1.33B business sale
data.description:
Gran Tierra Energy announced on Friday that stockholders approved the sale of its Colombian and Ecuadorian businesses to Maurel & Prom for approximately $1.33B.

The company expects to receive ~$315M in net cash proceeds, including $250M at closing and $65M payable 364 days later.

The deal still requires regulatory approvals in Colombia and Ecuador, with closing targeted for December 31, 2026.

data.title: Qualcomm and Arm jury to return next week after deliberations in contract dispute case
data.description:
Key points:
  • Qualcomm asks jury to find Arm intentionally interfered with Meta dealings by leaking 2024 breach letter
  • Qualcomm says Arm withheld software patches and design tools in breach of licensing agreements
  • Judge has not ruled on Qualcomm claim it could stop paying royalties for five years

By Tom Hals and Stephen Nellis

The jury in a lawsuit by chipmaker Qualcomm against chip technology supplier Arm Holdings did not reach a verdict on Friday as to whether Arm breached licensing agreements and intentionally sabotaged some of Qualcomm's dealings with Meta Platforms .

The five-day trial that wrapped up this week was the second in two years between the companies, highlighting the deterioration of their business relationship after SoftBank Group acquired control of Arm in 2016 and Arm shifted from licensing the technology needed to make chips to selling chips of its own.

At stake is whether Qualcomm, whose license for Arm's computing architecture runs until 2033, can eventually agree to terms for new versions of Arm's architecture.

After deliberating for about four hours Friday, the jury had not reached a verdict, indicating it would return to deliberations on Tuesday.

Qualcomm wants the jury to find that Arm breached its licensing agreements by withholding software patches and tools for its designs and by violating an agreement that was meant to ensure Qualcomm paid within 10% of the lowest price for Arm's processor designs.

It also wants the jury to find that Arm tried to torpedo Qualcomm's dealings with Meta by leaking to Bloomberg an Arm letter in 2024 notifying Qualcomm it was allegedly in breach of a key license agreement.

Arm's legal team this week tried to focus the jury on its claim that Qualcomm had not suffered any harm from the allegations in its lawsuit, which Arm cast as an attempt to exert leverage as the two fought over licensing terms. A related bench trial also took place this week over whether Arm is negotiating in good faith over those terms, though a decision on that could come well after Friday's verdict.

The trial in Wilmington, Delaware, federal court hinged on many of the same episodes as the 2024 trial in which Arm failed to convince a jury that Qualcomm had breached its licensing agreement with Arm. Both trials included testimony by both Arm CEO Rene Haas and Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon and were overseen by US District Judge Maryellen Noreika.

Qualcomm's lawyer Karen Dunn said in her opening statement that the case was very serious for the company.

"It’s really bad because Qualcomm’s entire chip business depends on Arm and on Arm honoring its contract and honoring its promises," she said on Monday.

Qualcomm wanted Noreika to rule prior to trial that a clause in the licensing agreements meant that Qualcomm could stop paying royalties for five years if the contract were breached. She has not issued her ruling, and Arm has argued the royalty penalty is unenforceable.

"They were not harmed in the least," Arm's attorney Gregg LoCascio told the jury on Monday.

data.title: CVS Stock Dips After Drop in Medicare Advantage Plan Ratings — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Catherine Dunn

Shares of CVS Health fell Friday after its insurance arm Aetna lost ground in the latest ratings of Medicare Advantage plans for seniors.

The stock was down 1.2%, while peer Humana, which made big gains in the ratings, was up 12% in late morning trading.

Insurance plans in the federal program are rated each year on a scale of one to five stars, summing up performance on dozens of quality measures. Seniors can view the star ratings as they shop this fall for next year's health coverage.

Wall Street tracks the ratings closely because plans that achieve four stars or more become eligible for bonus payments worth billions of dollars in total. The 2027 ratings will lead to bonuses in 2028, paid on a per-member basis.

The portion of Aetna membership in a four-star or higher plan shrank compared with last year, per the new 2027 ratings released Thursday after the market closed.

According to Aetna, about 69% of its members are in a 2027 plan with at least four stars, down from about 81% when the 2026 stars were first announced.

The ratings "came in weaker than expected" for CVS, said TD Cowen analyst Charles Rhyee in a research note Thursday evening. Rhyee estimated the "unmitigated impact" from lower year-over-year ratings at $720 million in 2028.

"While disappointing, we see potential for CVS to partially offset through benefit design," Rhyee wrote. "We expect additional color on the Stars outcome, mitigation opportunities, and sizable impacts" when CVS reports earnings for the third quarter.

Aetna President Steve Nelson said the insurer was "encouraged by our performance in areas like clinical quality and operational excellence" in the ratings.

Nelson said Aetna has "confidence in our ability to achieve our goal of returning to appropriate margins while at the same time driving continuous improvement and delivering even better experiences and outcomes for the members who count on us."

Raymond James analysts called ratings declines "relatively modest" at both CVS and UnitedHealth Group, and said the drops at both companies "can be largely mitigated through plan diversification by 2028."

UnitedHealth shares were up about 1% Friday morning.

data.title: CFTC Proposes to Expand Definition of Swaps to Include Prediction Markets Trading
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

The Commodity Futures Trading Commission is proposing to provide what it describes as additional clarity on the term "swap" that would include event contracts used in prediction market trading.

The expanded term would encompass event contracts on sporting, political, cultural and weather-related events, the CFTC said in a statement Friday.

The proposal notes that event contracts are financial instruments commonly known to trade as swaps.

The prediction markets industry, which is regulated by the CFTC, has been enmeshed in a debate about whether trading on events constitutes gambling, which would put it under the legal purview of states. The CFTC has said that the emerging industry is a form of financial trading, not betting.

"These products are commodity derivatives squarely within the CFTC's regulatory remit under the Commodity Exchange Act and are within the agency's exclusive jurisdiction," CFTC Chair Michael Selig said.

The agency is seeking public comment on the proposal. Comments must be submitted within 30 days.

Write to Katherine Hamilton at katherine.hamilton@wsj.com

data.title: Amazon shuffles Alexa leadership following high-end tablet release
data.description:
By Greg Bensinger

Amazon on Friday confirmed it was shuffling leadership in its Alexa division, a day after the company announced its first tablet computers featuring the voice assistant.

Daniel Rausch, a 17-year Amazon veteran who has served as vice president of Alexa and Echo for over three years, is stepping away from the unit next month, Amazon said in response to a Reuters inquiry.

Rausch, who has served as the face of Alexa at events and global launches, will return in another capacity in the devices and services division in 2027.

In his place, Amazon will install Aidan Marcuss, currently the vice president of Fire TV, advertising and the Amazon appstore. Marcuss joined Amazon from Microsoft in early 2025. He oversaw the release of a new Fire TV stick last month, which has garnered mixed reviews.

Kevin Keith, a product and marketing vice president, will keep that role but also take on Marcuss' responsibilities for the time being, Amazon said. The company declined to provide additional detail about the changes.

Alexa has been a consistent money-loser for Amazon since its release in 2014.

Amazon spent several years developing a new version of the voice assistant offering generative AI that can respond to longer prompts. The service is featured in the new Alexa Tablets announced on Thursday that Amazon has priced as a high-end product compared with prior Fire tablets that were inexpensive.

Alexa+, as the latest version is known, is included in the $139-per-year Prime membership or for $20 monthly as a standalone service.
